changes.reason: Ecce quantus ignis quam magnam silvam incendit contrasts a small fire with a great forest (cf. modicum membrum just before); the current sentence does not parse when read aloud.

changes.before: Or do you think that the scripture says in vain: To envy does the spirit covet which dwells in you?
changes.after: Or do you think that the scripture says in vain: The spirit which dwells in you covets to the point of envy?
changes.reason: Ad invidiam concupiscit spiritus qui habitat in vobis means the indwelling spirit covets unto envy; the inverted Douay order “To envy does the spirit covet” is very hard to follow aloud.

changes.before: Detract not one another, my brothers. He that slanders his brother, or he that judges his brother, slanders the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge.
changes.after: Do not slander one another, brothers. He that slanders his brother, or he that judges his brother, slanders the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge.
changes.reason: Nolite detrahere alterutrum fratres uses the same verb the verse then renders “slander” (detrahit); “Detract not one another” is unclear aloud, and the Latin has fratres without mei.

changes.before: For what is your life? It is a vapour which appears for a little while and afterwards shall vanish away. For that you should say: If the Lord will, and, If we shall live, we will do this or that.
changes.after: For what is your life? It is a vapour which appears for a little while and afterwards shall vanish away. Instead you ought to say: If the Lord will, and, If we shall live, we will do this or that.
changes.reason: Pro eo ut dicatis means “instead of which you ought to say”; the archaic “For that you should say” is misheard as giving a reason.

changes.before: Go to now, you rich men: weep and howl in your miseries, which shall come upon you.
changes.after: Come now, you rich men: weep and howl in your miseries, which shall come upon you.
changes.reason: Agite nunc is the summons “come now”; the archaic Douay “Go to now” trips a modern listener.

changes.before: Your gold and silver is cankered: and the rust of them shall be for a testimony against you and shall eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up to yourselves wrath against the last days.
changes.after: Your gold and silver have rusted: and the rust of them shall be for a testimony against you and shall eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up to yourselves wrath in the last days.
changes.reason: Aeruginavit is “has rusted” (as the following aerugo, “rust,” shows), and thesaurizastis vobis iram in novissimis diebus says the wrath was stored up in the last days, not “against” them.

changes.before: Elijah was a man passible like to us: and with prayer he prayed that it might not rain upon the earth. And it rained not for three years and six months.
changes.after: Elijah was a man subject to suffering like us: and with prayer he prayed that it might not rain upon the earth. And it rained not for three years and six months.
changes.reason: Similis nobis passibilis means a man capable of suffering, like us; “passible like to us” is an archaism a listener will not catch.

changes.before: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has regenerated us to a lively hope, by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead:
changes.after: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has regenerated us to a living hope, by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead:
changes.reason: Spem vivam is a living hope; in modern English “lively” means energetic, which misleads when heard.

changes.before: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle but also to the froward.
changes.after: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle but also to the harsh.
changes.reason: Dyscolis means difficult or harsh masters; the Douay “froward” is an archaism most listeners will not understand.

changes.before: And in fine, be all of one mind, having compassion one of another, being lovers of the brotherhood, merciful, modest, humble:
changes.after: And finally, be all of one mind, having compassion one of another, being lovers of the brotherhood, merciful, modest, humble:
changes.reason: In fine means “finally”; heard aloud, “in fine” sounds like “fine” and trips the listener.

changes.before: For the time is, that judgment should begin at the house of God. And if at first at us, what shall be the end of them that believe not the gospel of God?
changes.after: For the time is, that judgment should begin at the house of God. And if it begins first with us, what shall be the end of them that believe not the gospel of God?
changes.reason: Si autem primum a nobis means “and if it begins first with us” (judgment, from the previous clause); “And if at first at us” is hard to follow aloud.

changes.before: The ancients therefore that are among you, I implore who am myself also an ancient and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, as also a partaker of that glory which is to be revealed in time to come:
changes.after: The elders therefore that are among you, I implore who am myself also an elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, as also a partaker of that glory which is to be revealed in time to come:
changes.reason: Seniores … consenior are the church’s elders (the column already writes “The elder” for Senior in 2 John 1 and 3 John 1); “the ancients” sounds aloud like very old or long-dead people.

changes.before: In like manner, you young men, be subject to the ancients. And do you all insinuate humility one to another: for God resists the proud, but to the humble he gives grace.
changes.after: In like manner, you young men, be subject to the elders. And all of you, show humility to one another: for God resists the proud, but to the humble he gives grace.
changes.reason: Senioribus are the elders of 5:1, and humilitatem insinuate means to put on or show humility toward one another; in modern English “insinuate” means to hint slyly, which misleads.

changes.before: Whom resist you, strong in faith: knowing that the same affliction befalls, your brothers who are in the world.
changes.after: Resist him, strong in faith: knowing that the same affliction befalls your brothers who are in the world.
changes.reason: Eamdem passionem … vestrae fraternitati fieri means the same affliction befalls your brotherhood; the comma after “befalls” makes “your brothers” sound like an address, and “Whom resist you” is archaic.

changes.before: But I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance.
changes.after: But I think it right, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance.
changes.reason: Justum arbitror means “I think it right”; the archaic “meet” trips a listener (it sounds like “meet” or “mete”).

changes.before: And I will endeavour that you frequently have after my decease whereby you may keep a memory of these things.
changes.after: And I will endeavour that after my decease you may frequently have the means to keep these things in memory.
changes.reason: Dabo operam et frequenter habere vos post obitum meum, ut horum memoriam faciatis means Peter will see to it that after his death they can often call these things to mind; the Douay word order does not parse when read aloud.

changes.before: I heard what seemed a voice among the four living creatures saying, “Two Roman pounds of wheat for a denarius, and three measures of two Roman pounds of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the wine and the oil.”
changes.after: I heard what seemed a voice among the four living creatures saying, “A measure of two Roman pounds of wheat for a denarius, and three such measures of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the wine and the oil.”
changes.reason: Bilibris is one two-pound measure; the phrase “three measures of two Roman pounds of barley” is hard to follow aloud, so the measure is stated once and reused.
